definitions.explanation: A written or inscribed charm believed to ward off evil, illness, or misfortune through spiritual power.

examples.japanese: {護符|ごふ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{身|み}につける→身につける：03158_minitsukeru⟧。
⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{護符|ごふ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦いただいた→いただく：01326_itadaku⟧。
examples.english: I received a protective charm at the shrine.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧{護符|ごふ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{柱|はしら}→柱：05009_hashira⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{貼|は}ってあった→貼る：10447_haru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}つけた→見つける：01180_mitsukeru⟧。
examples.english: I found an old talisman stuck to a pillar in the house.

notes:
A {護符|ごふ} is typically a strip of paper or wood inscribed with sacred characters, prayers, or symbols. Unlike {お守|まも}り (which is usually a fabric pouch), {護符|ごふ} specifically refers to the written or printed charm itself.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {護符|ごふ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{貼|は}る→貼る：10447_haru⟧: to affix a talisman (to a door, pillar, etc.)
- {護符|ごふ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{身|み}につける→身につける：03158_minitsukeru⟧: to carry a talisman on one's person
- {護符|ごふ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{授|さず}かる→授かる：12797_sazukaru⟧: to receive a talisman (from a temple or shrine)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {お守|まも}り: amulet, charm (usually a fabric pouch from a shrine)
- ⟦{札|ふだ}→札：23002_fuda⟧: paper charm, talisman (general term)
- {呪符|じゅふ}: spell tag (emphasis on magical power)
